portInfo.description: Wellington’s cruise passengers land at CentrePort, which publishes a dedicated cruise passenger zone and city shuttle rules. The cruise-line information page states over 900 m of dedicated quay berth with in-house gangways and marine services. Queens Wharf is a separate city waterfront facility — not treated as the CentrePort cruise door here.
portInfo.location: Located at southern tip of North Island, New Zealand

facts.significance: Capital city and cultural hub of New Zealand

climate.description: Windy maritime climate with moderate temperatures

politics.visaRequirements: Visa or NZeTA required for most visitors. Visa waiver for some nationalities.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. NZeTA or visa required for most visitors.

gettingThere.walkingTime: 10-15 minutes to city center—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.
gettingThere.publicTransport: Cruise shuttle to Wakefield Street (2026/27 season). No public access and no taxi pickup on the berth. Airport 8.5 km.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Cuba Street — short walk from shuttle area.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Arrange city meetups off-port — no public/taxi access at the berth.
